title: NaviMed-UMB: hardware envelope studies for local AI deployment on consumer RDNA 4 GPUs

creators.name: Minarowski, Łukasz
creators.affiliation: Department of Respiratory Physiopathology, Medical University of Białystok, Poland

description:
NaviMed-UMB is an engineering log and a reproducible benchmark suite. It measures how modern open-weight large language models run on a consumer workstation with two AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB cards (gfx1201, RDNA 4, Navi 48), under ROCm 7.2 and vLLM 0.19. The repository is the first layer (engineering and hardware envelope) of the three-layer NaviMed programme for sovereign, on-premise medical AI.

The project provides a benchmark protocol with explicit Phase 1 and Phase 2 gates and a strict embargo classification (METHODOLOGY §11). It also provides per-model software and hardware manifests, and public engineering envelopes (§11.1) for a 21-model suite. AWQ W4A16 releases of the Polish PLLuM family are published on Hugging Face under mozarcik/ (8B on a Llama base, 12B on a Mistral-Nemo base, 70B on a Llama base). The 8B and 12B models were quantised on the R9700 workstation, and the 70B family on an AMD Instinct MI300X through the AMD Developer Cloud, powered by DigitalOcean, under the AMD Developer Program. A Polish calibration corpus is released as well: mozarcik/clinical-pl-smpc-awq-calibration, 418 fragments of European Medicines Agency drug information, with no patient data.

Version 0.5.2 changes how power is reported and corrects two provenance records. Power is now the sum of both cards in each 1 Hz sample. Averaging the cards, as before, understated the system draw by a factor of two on this machine. The power window is now the generation phase only, so energy per token no longer includes model loading and warmup.

Each run now stores the kernel command line. The whole campaign ran with the IOMMU in its default translating mode, which matters because iommu=pt changes host-to-GPU transfers. Sixty added runs (three configurations, TP=1 and TP=2, ten repetitions) complete the BF16/AWQ pairs at a single stream, so the precision ratio is now defined at N = 1. Multiple-comparison correction covers eight concurrency levels, from N = 1 to N = 1000.

The work is meant for researchers building local AI infrastructure for sensitive data, for hardware reviewers, maintainers of RDNA 4 support in inference frameworks, and clinical-AI groups evaluating Polish models.
notes: AI assistance disclosure: this project is developed with generative-AI assistance (Anthropic Claude via claude.ai and the Claude Code agentic command-line tool; OpenAI GPT and Google Gemini via web apps; open-weight models served locally on the project's R9700 workstation for Polish-language proofreading). Claude Code runs on the measurement workstation under the author's supervision and, in some sessions, launched author-approved scripts and benchmark runs; no AI tool generated, estimated or interpolated a measurement.
